mainTopic: Mentioning שבת in נעילה; the new משנה on oils for lighting; why קדשים are not burned on יום טוב
overview: The גמרא ends its discussion of which special days get mentioned in prayers. It rules like רבי יהושע בן לוי: when יום הכיפורים falls on שבת, you mention שבת even in נעילה, because the day itself requires four prayers. It then answers a seeming contradiction from רבא: the חזן's Friday-night repetition was added by the חכמים only for safety, so it is not a true prayer of the day. Next the גמרא explains that in the משנה about lighting with אליה, the חכמים and the תנא קמא argue over רב ברונא's ruling, though we cannot tell who holds which side. A new משנה follows. It forbids lighting with שמן שריפה on יום טוב, and it records a dispute about which oils may be used for שבת lights: רבי ישמעאל forbids tar, the חכמים permit all oils, and רבי טרפון allows only olive oil. The גמרא explains that the rule about שמן שריפה comes from a general principle that קדשים are not burned on יום טוב. It then brings sources for that principle from חזקיה, אביי and רבא. רב אשי begins a fourth source, from the word 'שבתון', which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The final ruling: mention שבת in נעילה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects all the earlier opinions and rules like רבי יהושע בן לוי: on יום הכיפורים that falls on שבת, נעילה must mention שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The הלכה does not follow any of these teachings. Instead, it follows רבי יהושע בן לוי: when יום הכיפורים falls on שבת, whoever prays נעילה must mention שבת, because this is a day that is obligated in four prayers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up the earlier debate about mentioning a special day in a prayer that does not normally belong to it. It gives the final הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נעילה is not said on a regular שבת, so you might think שבת has nothing to do with it. רבי יהושע בן לוי says that does not matter. יום הכיפורים itself requires four prayers, so each of them is a full prayer of that day, and every holiness present that day, including שבת, gets mentioned in it.

keyTerms.meaning: The halacha, the practical ruling
Teachings or rulings (here, the earlier opinions)
The closing prayer of יום הכיפורים
To mention (insert into the prayer)
Four prayers: שחרית, מוסף, מנחה, נעילה

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical הלכה: on a יום הכיפורים that falls on שבת, שבת is mentioned in נעילה.

phrases.english: And the halacha is not like any of these teachings,
rather, it is like that which was said by
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi:
Yom Kippur that falls on Shabbat —
one who prays Neilah
must mention Shabbat.
It is a day that is obligated in four prayers.
phrases.notes: The day itself requires נעילה, so נעילה is a true prayer of the day.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵית הִילְכְתָא כְּכׇל הָנֵי שְׁמַעְתָּתָא, אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the earlier debate (on the previous amud) about mentioning a special day in extra prayers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On יום הכיפורים that falls on שבת, שבת is mentioned in נעילה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The halacha follows רבי יהושע בן לוי, because the day itself is obligated in four prayers.

steps.title: Contradiction from רבא's ruling on Friday-night repetition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ruling: we also rule like רבא, who says the חזן does not mention יום טוב in the Friday-night repetition, which seems to contradict רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: One הלכה contradicts another הלכה! You said the הלכה follows רבי יהושע בן לוי, but we hold the הלכה follows רבא. רבא said: when יום טוב falls on שבת, the שליח ציבור who goes down before the ark for the evening prayer does not mention יום טוב, because if it were not שבת, the שליח ציבור would not go down for the evening prayer on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out two accepted rulings that seem to clash. רבא seems to say that a prayer created only because of one holiness (שבת) does not mention the other holiness (יום טוב).
steps.deeperAnalysis: On Friday night the חזן repeats a short version of the עמידה (מגן אבות), but only because it is שבת, not because of יום טוב. So רבא says יום טוב is not mentioned in it. By the same logic, נעילה exists only because of יום הכיפורים, so שבת should not be mentioned in it, the opposite of רבי יהושע בן לוי.

keyTerms.meaning: One halacha contradicts another halacha
We hold (an accepted ruling)
The prayer leader (חזן)
Goes down before the ark (leads the prayer)
If it were not for

steps.confusionAlert: The 'evening prayer' here is not the regular silent עמידה. It is the חזן's short repetition on Friday night (ברכה מעין שבע), which is only said on שבת.

phrases.english: One halacha contradicts another halacha!

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרַתְּ הִילְכְתָא כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי,
phrases.english: You said the halacha is like Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi,
and we hold the halacha is like Rava.
For Rava said:
A Festival that falls on Shabbat,

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלִיחַ צִיבּוּר הַיּוֹרֵד לִפְנֵי הַתֵּיבָה עַרְבִית
phrases.english: the prayer leader who goes down before the ark in the evening

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לְהַזְכִּיר שֶׁל יוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: need not mention the Festival,
because if it were not Shabbat,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין שְׁלִיחַ צִבּוּר יוֹרֵד עַרְבִית בְּיוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: the prayer leader would not go down in the evening on a Festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling of Step 1 using another accepted ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling like רבי יהושע בן לוי that שבת is mentioned in נעילה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא holds that a prayer that exists only because of one holiness does not mention another holiness. נעילה exists only because of יום הכיפורים, so by רבא's logic שבת should not be mentioned in it.

steps.title: The cases are different: safety enactment vs. obligation of the day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the comparison. The Friday-night repetition is a rabbinic safety measure and not a real prayer of the day, while נעילה is an obligation of the day itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare them? There, by strict law, even on שבת no repetition is needed. It was the חכמים who instituted it because of danger. But here, it is a day that is obligated in four prayers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by showing the two cases are not alike, so both rulings stand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Friday-night repetition is not a true prayer of שבת. The חכמים added it so latecomers would not walk home alone in the dark from בתי כנסת outside the city. Since it is not a prayer of the day, it does not pull in יום טוב. נעילה, however, is a real obligation of the day, so it is a full prayer and includes everything special about that day, including שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? (rejecting a comparison)
By strict law
They instituted (a rabbinic enactment)
Danger

steps.whatToRemember: A prayer that comes from the day's own obligation (like נעילה) mentions every holiness of the day. A prayer added for an outside reason (like the Friday-night repetition, added for safety) does not.

phrases.english: How can you compare?!
There, by strict law,
even on Shabbat it is also not needed,
and it was the Rabbis who instituted it because of danger.
But here —
it is a day that is obligated in four prayers.
phrases.notes: The גמרא repeats רבי יהושע בן לוי's reason, now to show how נעילה differs from the safety-based repetition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both cases looked alike: a special prayer created by one holiness, with a second holiness also present.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Friday-night repetition is only a rabbinic safety measure and not a prayer of the day, while נעילה is required by the day itself. So רבא and רבי יהושע בן לוי do not conflict.

steps.title: How do the חכמים differ from the תנא קמא on lighting with אליה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה about not lighting with sheep's-tail fat and asks why the חכמים are listed separately when they seem to say the same thing as the תנא קמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And not with a sheep's tail, etc.' The חכמים are the same as the תנא קמא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic by quoting the משנה about oils for שבת candles. It points out that the חכמים seem to repeat the תנא קמא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's first, unnamed opinion forbids lighting with אליה and חלב. נחום המדי permits cooked fat. The חכמים then forbid fat whether cooked or not, which sounds identical to the תנא קמא. A משנה does not normally repeat the same opinion twice, so the גמרא asks what the difference is.

keyTerms.meaning: The fatty tail of a sheep
Etc. (the quote continues)
The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה
That is the same as

phrases.english: "And not with a sheep's tail, etc."
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה: not with sheep's tail and not with fat. נחום המדי permits cooked fat; the חכמים forbid it whether cooked or not.

phrases.english: The Rabbis are the same as the first tanna!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: returns to analyzing the משנה about lighting materials.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of the משנה, which lists the חכמים separately from the תנא קמא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the two opinions are identical, the משנה should not list them as two separate views.

steps.title: They differ over רב ברונא's ruling, but we don't know who holds which side
steps.stepSummary: The difference between the תנא קמא and the חכמים is רב ברונא's ruling in the name of רב, that cooked fat with a little oil added may be used. We cannot tell which of them permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is the ruling of רב ברונא in the name of רב. And it is not clear which one holds which view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two opinions do differ. They argue about whether cooked fat mixed with a little oil may be used for the candles.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רב ברונא quoted רב that cooked fat with some oil added may be lit. One of the two opinions (תנא קמא or חכמים) agrees with this and the other forbids it. The גמרא admits it cannot identify which is which.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them
An אמורא who quoted רב on cooked fat with oil
They are not identified (we don't know who holds what)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not try to figure out which opinion permits the mixture. The גמרא itself says this is unknown. It only establishes that a real disagreement exists.

phrases.english: The difference between them is
the ruling that Rav Beruna said in the name of Rav.
phrases.notes: Cooked fat with a little oil added may be used for lighting.

phrases.english: And it is not defined who holds which view.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 4 by naming the practical difference.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תנא קמא and the חכמים seemed to say exactly the same thing.
steps.terutzMaskana: They argue about רב ברונא's case of cooked fat mixed with oil, but which one permits it is not known.

steps.title: The משנה: no lighting with burnable impure oil on a Festival
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that one may not light a lamp with שמן שריפה on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One may not light with oil that is meant to be burned on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. Its first rule is that oil which must be destroyed by burning may not be used for lighting on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמן שריפה is תרומה oil that became impure (טמא). It may not be eaten, so the halacha is to burn it, and using it as lamp fuel is the normal way of doing that. The משנה says this burning may not be done on יום טוב. The גמרא will explain why in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה. This marks the start of the משנה text.
Oil for burning. This is תרומה oil that became impure and must be burned.
A Festival day
We light (a lamp)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not translate שמן שריפה as 'oil that was already burnt' or 'used oil.' It is impure תרומה oil that is waiting to be burned.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One may not light with oil designated for burning
on a Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין מַדְלִיקִין בְּשֶׁמֶן שְׂרֵיפָה בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the previous discussion about sheep's-tail fat ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lighting with שמן שריפה on יום טוב is forbidden.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל forbids tar, while the חכמים permit all oils
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל forbids lighting שבת lamps with עטרן (tar) out of respect for שבת. The חכמים permit all oils and list many examples, including tar and naphtha.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל says: We do not light with tar, out of respect for שבת. The חכמים allow all oils: sesame oil, nut oil, turnip oil, fish oil, gourd oil, tar, and naphtha.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה turns to שבת lights. It records a disagreement about whether bad-smelling fuels like tar may be used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל's concern is כבוד שבת. Tar smells bad, and a bad smell spoils the pleasant atmosphere of שבת. The חכמים do not worry about this: any oil that burns properly is acceptable, even tar and naphtha.

keyTerms.meaning: Tar, a sticky fuel with a bad smell
Honor and respect for שבת
Naphtha, a petroleum-type fuel
The Sages permit

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael says:
one may not light with tar
out of respect for Shabbat.
And the Rabbis permit all oils:
sesame oil, nut oil,
turnip oil, fish oil,
gourd oil, tar, and naphtha.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר אֵין מַדְלִיקִין בְּעִטְרָן מִפְּנֵי כְּבוֹד הַשַּׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה, moving from יום טוב to the oils used for שבת lights.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי ישמעאל forbids tar because of כבוד שבת. The חכמים permit all oils, including tar and naphtha.

steps.title: רבי טרפון allows only olive oil
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון takes the strictest view: only olive oil may be used for שבת lights.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי טרפון says: We light only with olive oil.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes with a third opinion, which is stricter than both earlier ones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל ruled out only tar. רבי טרפון rules out everything except olive oil, which is the best and most pleasant oil. This gives the משנה a full range of opinions, from most lenient (חכמים) to most strict (רבי טרפון).

keyTerms.meaning: Olive oil
Only, exclusively

phrases.english: Rabbi Tarfon says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מַדְלִיקִין אֶלָּא בְּשֶׁמֶן זַיִת בִּלְבַד.
phrases.english: One may light only with olive oil.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן אוֹמֵר אֵין מַדְלִיקִין אֶלָּא בְּשֶׁמֶן זַיִת בִּלְבַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third and stricter opinion to the dispute about oils for שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only olive oil may be used for שבת lights.

steps.title: Why is burnable oil forbidden on a Festival?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins and asks for the reason behind the משנה's first rule about שמן שריפה on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the first rule of the משנה and asks why it is forbidden. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lighting a lamp on יום טוב is normally allowed. So why should this particular oil be a problem? The גמרא wants the underlying principle.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: GEMARA:
What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the rule in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason one may not light with שמן שריפה on יום טוב.

steps.title: Because consecrated items are not burned on a Festival
steps.stepSummary: The reason is a general rule: we do not burn קדשים on יום טוב. Impure תרומה oil falls under this rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because we do not burn holy items on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this is one example of a bigger rule: holy things that must be destroyed by burning are not burned on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Burning impure תרומה is a מצוה of destroying a holy item. It is not cooking or preparing food. The work allowed on יום טוב is only work done for eating, so this kind of burning has to wait until a weekday.

keyTerms.meaning: We burn
Consecrated or holy items (here, including תרומה)

phrases.english: Because one may not burn consecrated items
on a Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין שׂוֹרְפִין קׇדָשִׁים בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: There is a general prohibition against burning קדשים on יום טוב.
steps.whyThisMatters: This general rule is the foundation for the whole rest of this passage. Every source the גמרא brings next is a proof of this principle.

steps.title: What is the source for this rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that קדשים may not be burned on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a פסוק behind the rule it just stated. This sets up three different answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule 'we do not burn קדשים on יום טוב' was stated without proof. The גמרא now wants a Torah source for it.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these words (learned)? A request for a source.

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the Torah source of the principle stated in step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source showing that קדשים may not be burned on יום טוב.

steps.title: חזקיה: the extra 'עד בקר' gives a second morning for burning
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה, and also a ברייתא from his study house, learn the rule from the extra words 'עד בקר' in the פסוק about leftover קרבן פסח. The Torah is pointing to a second morning for burning the leftovers, which shows the burning may not happen on יום טוב itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה said, and the study house of חזקיה taught the same: The פסוק says, 'Do not leave any of it until morning, and what is left of it until morning, burn in fire.' The Torah did not need to say 'until morning' again. Why does it say it? To give a second morning for burning it.
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיה gives the first source, from the קרבן פסח. Its leftover meat is not burned on the first morning, which is יום טוב, but on the next morning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second 'until morning' looks unnecessary, so it must teach something. The leftovers are found on the morning of the 15th, which is יום טוב, yet the Torah says to burn them at a later morning, the 16th. This shows that burning קדשים is not done on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching (ברייתא) from the study house of חזקיה
The פסוק says
Leftover sacrificial meat
The Torah did not need to say this (so it must come to teach something)
A second morning

phrases.english: Ḥizkiya said,
and so it was taught in the school of Ḥizkiya:
the verse said:
"And you shall leave nothing of it until morning;
and what remains of it until morning" (you shall burn).
The Torah did not need to say "until morning" again!
Why does it say "until morning"?
The verse comes to give him
a second morning for its burning.
phrases.notes: The 16th of ניסן, after יום טוב

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר חִזְקִיָּה וְכֵן תָּנָא דְּבֵי חִזְקִיָּה אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the source question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra 'עד בקר' in the פסוק about leftover קרבן פסח pushes the burning to a second morning, after יום טוב.

steps.title: אביי: the שבת offering is brought only on שבת
steps.stepSummary: אביי gives a different source: 'עולת שבת בשבתו' teaches that weekday offerings are not brought on שבת or on יום טוב. Burning קדשים is a weekday-type task, so it is also excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The פסוק says, 'The burnt offering of שבת on its שבת.' This means only the שבת offering is brought on שבת, not a weekday offering on שבת, and not a weekday offering on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי offers a second, alternative source for the same rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק limits what is done on the holy day to the offering belonging to that day. אביי extends the limit from שבת to יום טוב as well. Burning leftover or impure קדשים is not a מצוה of the day itself, so it is pushed off to a weekday.

keyTerms.meaning: The burnt offering of שבת on its שבת (במדבר כח:י)
A weekday burnt offering

phrases.english: Abaye said: the verse said:
"The burnt offering of Shabbat on its Shabbat":
and not a weekday burnt offering on Shabbat,
and not a weekday burnt offering on a Festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative source to חזקיה's derivation.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that קדשים are not burned on יום טוב.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'עולת שבת בשבתו' limits what is offered on a holy day to that day's own offering. That excludes weekday offerings on שבת and on יום טוב, so burning קדשים is excluded too.

steps.title: רבא: 'that alone may be done for you' limits Festival work
steps.stepSummary: רבא learns the rule from 'הוא לבדו יעשה לכם.' 'הוא' excludes preparations for food (מכשירין), and 'לבדו' excludes a ברית מילה that is not on its proper day, even though one might have allowed it through a קל וחומר. Likewise, burning קדשים is not permitted on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The פסוק says, 'Only that alone may be done for you.' 'That' means food itself, not the preparations for it. 'Alone' means not a מילה done after its proper time, which we might otherwise have permitted through a קל וחומר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a third source, from the פסוק that permits food-related work on יום טוב. He reads it as a strict limit on what is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק allows work on יום טוב only for food. Each limiting word cuts something out: 'הוא' removes food preparations, and 'לבדו' removes even a מצוה like a late מילה. If a מצוה like a late מילה is not allowed, then burning קדשים, which is also not a מצוה of the day, is certainly not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Only that alone may be done for you (שמות יב:טז)
Preparations that make food-work possible (like making tools)
A ברית מילה not done on its proper day (the eighth day)
A logical argument from a lighter case to a stricter one

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה forbids lighting with שמן שריפה on יום טוב because we do not burn קדשים on יום טוב. The גמרא gives sources for this: חזקיה (the second 'עד בקר' about the קרבן פסח), אביי ('עולת שבת בשבתו'), and רבא ('הוא לבדו'). The next step begins a fourth source from רב אשי.
steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'דאתיא בקל וחומר' does not mean the late מילה IS permitted by a קל וחומר. It means one might have permitted it that way, so the Torah needed the word 'לבדו' to forbid it.

phrases.english: Rava said: the verse said:
"That alone may be done for you."
"That": but not food preparations (facilitators).
"Alone": and not a circumcision not at its proper time,
which could have been derived (as permitted) through an a fortiori argument.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a third, alternative source after חזקיה and אביי.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that קדשים are not burned on יום טוב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק 'הוא לבדו יעשה לכם' (שמות יב:טז) and its limiting words.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The limiting words 'הוא לבדו' in the פסוק about work on יום טוב exclude מכשירין and even a מילה שלא בזמנה. So burning קדשים, which is not a מצוה of the day, is excluded too.

steps.title: רב אשי begins a new source from the word 'שבתון'
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי offers a fourth source for the rule against burning קדשים on יום טוב. He points to the word 'שבתון', which the Torah uses when describing יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי opens a new, fourth source for why קדשים are not burned on יום טוב by pointing to the Torah's word 'שבתון'. This is only his opening line, setting up an explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each earlier source (חזקיה's 'עד בקר', אביי's 'עולת שבת בשבתו', רבא's 'הוא לבדו') came from a different פסוק. רב אשי moves to yet another word: 'שבתון', the Torah's term for a day of rest on יום טוב. The parentheses show a text correction: the printed version read 'שבת', but the correct reading is 'שבתון'.

keyTerms.meaning: A later אמורא who gives his own fourth source for the rule
'A day of rest': the Torah's word for יום טוב, used here as the source

steps.confusionAlert: The word in parentheses, 'שבת', is not part of רב אשי's statement. It is an older printed reading that was corrected. רב אשי's actual word is 'שבתון', taken here from the פסוקים about יום טוב (ויקרא כג:כד).

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
(Not 'Shabbat' but) 'Shabbaton', a day of rest:
phrases.notes: Some versions have 'שבת' in round brackets, but the corrected wording is 'שבתון' (ויקרא כג:כד). The dash means the explanation continues on the next lines.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of sources answering Step 11's question. After רבא's source in Step 14, רב אשי offers a fourth, independent derivation.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that קדשים may not be burned on יום טוב
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word 'שבתון' in the פסוקים about יום טוב (ויקרא כג:כד). The full reasoning follows on the next amud.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב אשי derives the rule from the word 'שבתון' used for יום טוב. His full reasoning continues on the next amud.
